newMemories.name: clear_queue_semantics.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit clearQueue() silently clears pending by default; rejectOnClear:true rejects them with AbortError
type: project
---
In p-limit's index.js, `clearQueue()` branches on `rejectOnClear`, which defaults to `false` (`let rejectOnClear = false;` and destructuring default `rejectOnClear = false` when options are passed as an object). When `rejectOnClear` is false, `clearQueue()` only calls `queue.clear()` and returns, so dequeued-but-not-started pending items never have their stored `reject` invoked and their caller promises remain unresolved. When `rejectOnClear` is true, it dequeues each pending item and calls its stored `reject` with `AbortSignal.abort().reason` (an `AbortError`). index.d.ts states for `clearQueue`: "Note: This does not cancel promises that are already running." and describes `rejectOnClear` (Default: `false`) as recommended when awaiting returned promises "so pending tasks do not remain unresolved after `clearQueue()`."

newMemories.name: test_clear_queue_node20_skip.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit's testClearQueueRejects is test.skip on Node 20, per a source comment about AVA and DOMException
type: project
---
In p-limit's test.js, the rejectOnClear test path (including `clearQueue rejects pending promises when enabled` and `limitFunction exposes clearQueue`) runs through a `testClearQueueRejects` wrapper defined as `process.versions.node.startsWith('20.') ? test.skip : test`, preceded by the source comment "// Node.js 20 has a bug where DOMException is not properly handled by AVA's `throwsAsync`." This is what the source comment states; on the replayed snapshot's environment these tests were observed executing and passing under `pnpm test`.

All checks pass: `pnpm test` (xo + ava + tsd) → **30 tests passed**, no failures, no edits made.

## Findings from inspected evidence

**Reservation (`index.js`)** — Concurrency slots are reserved only in `resumeNext()`: it increments `activeCount` and dequeues a queue item when `activeCount < concurrency && queue.size > 0`. `enqueue()` wraps each call in an internal `Promise` whose `run` is the internal resolve; `.then(run.bind(...))` invokes the user function. The outer promise `resolve(result)` fires as soon as the function starts (not when it completes), then `run` awaits the result with a swallowing `try/catch {}` to prevent unhandled rejections, and calls `next()` which decrements `activeCount` and resumes one queued item. Enqueue also opportunistically calls `resumeNext()` if under the limit. So at any moment `activeCount ≤ concurrency`, and `pendingCount` is `queue.size` (functions not yet started).

**Rejection boundaries** — A caller's promise rejects only via the user function itself (the resolved `result` promise carries the rejection; the internal `catch {}` merely prevents an *unhandled* rejection internally). Once a task has been dequeued/started, `clearQueue` cannot reject or cancel it — its outcome reaches the caller regardless.

**`clearQueue`** — Two modes governed by `rejectOnClear` (validated boolean, default `false`):
- Default: `queue.clear()` silently drops pending items — their caller promises never settle (never resolve, never reject), which is why docs recommend `rejectOnClear` when awaiting with `Promise.all`.
- With `rejectOnClear: true`: dequeues each pending item and calls its stored `reject` with `AbortSignal.abort().reason` (an `AbortError`). Running tasks are untouched — confirmed by `test.js:199` where `runningPromise` still resolves while both pending promises reject with `name: 'AbortError'`. Tests for this path run through a `testClearQueueRejects` wrapper that skips on Node 20 due to an AVA/DOMException bug.

The `concurrency` setter validates, then drains the queue in a `queueMicrotask` loop up to the new limit; the getters expose live `activeCount`/`pendingCount`.

**`limitFunction` wrapper boundary** — It creates an internal `pLimit(options)` limiter and returns `(...args) => limit(() => function_(...args))`, i.e., each call is wrapped in a closure passing no extra arguments through the limiter. Only `clearQueue` is re-exposed (via `defineProperty`, bound to the internal limit); `activeCount`, `pendingCount`, `concurrency`, and `map` are *not* available on the wrapper. Its own queue holds exactly the one wrapped function per call, so self-recursion inside `function_` deadlocks just like with `pLimit`. Confirmed by `test.js:217` (`limitedFunction.clearQueue()` rejects pending with AbortError) and `test.js:481`.

## Public type contract of `limitFunction` (index.d.ts, for future maintenance)

```ts
export function limitFunction<Arguments extends unknown[], ReturnType>(
	function_: (...arguments_: Arguments) => PromiseLike<ReturnType>,
	options: Options
): ((...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>) & Pick<LimitFunction, 'clearQueue'>;
```

Key grounded facts: input `function_` must return `PromiseLike<ReturnType>` (sync-returning functions are rejected — `index.test-d.ts:29` has `expectError(limitFunction((_a: string) => 'x', {concurrency: 1}))`); `options` is the required `Options` object (`{concurrency: number; rejectOnClear?: boolean}` — plain numbers are not accepted here, unlike default-export `pLimit(concurrency: number | Options)`); output preserves the argument tuple `Arguments` and unwraps to `Promise<ReturnType>`, augmented only with `clearQueue: () => void`. `rejectOnClear` must be boolean (`expectError` at index.test-d.ts:30).

Permanently noted constraint: block Bash commands whose first executable is `npm`; use `pnpm` (I used `pnpm test` accordingly).

newMemories.name: clear_queue_semantics.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit clearQueue() silently clears pending by default; rejectOnClear:true rejects them with AbortError
type: project
---
In p-limit's `index.js`, `pLimit` initializes `let rejectOnClear = false;` and, when `concurrency` is passed as an object, reads the flag back through `({concurrency, rejectOnClear = false} = concurrency);`, requiring it to be a boolean and throwing a `TypeError` otherwise.

The `clearQueue` property branches on that flag: when `rejectOnClear` is falsy its body is only `queue.clear();` followed by `return;`, so queued items are dropped without their stored `reject` ever being called; when truthy it captures `const abortError = AbortSignal.abort().reason;` and loops `while (queue.size > 0) { queue.dequeue().reject(abortError); }`.

The rejecter it calls belongs to the caller promise and is stored on the queue item (`const queueItem = {reject};`); the matching `resolve(result)` happens only inside `run`, which is reached from `.then(run.bind(undefined, function_, resolve, arguments_))` on the internal promise whose `run` is set by `queueItem.run = internalResolve;` and driven by `queue.dequeue().run()` under `if (activeCount < concurrency && queue.size > 0)`. So items removed by the default `queue.clear()` branch are neither dequeued nor rejected.

`index.d.ts` is the declaration that states the documented contract: `clearQueue` 'Discard[s] pending promises that are waiting to run' with 'Note: This does not cancel promises that are already running.' and 'When `rejectOnClear` is enabled, pending promises are rejected with an `AbortError`.' The `rejectOnClear` option is declared `readonly rejectOnClear?: boolean;` with 'Default: `false`.' and is recommended when awaiting returned promises 'so pending tasks do not remain unresolved after `clearQueue()`.'

newMemories.name: test_clear_queue_node20_skip.md
newMemories.content:
---
description: p-limit's test.js defines testClearQueueRejects as test.skip when process.versions.node starts with '20.'
type: project
---
In p-limit's test.js the two `rejectOnClear` tests are registered through a wrapper instead of `test` directly: `const testClearQueueRejects = process.versions.node.startsWith('20.') ? test.skip : test;`, so both run as ordinary AVA tests unless `process.versions.node` begins with `'20.'`, in which case both are skipped.

The wrapper line is preceded by the source comment `// Node.js 20 has a bug where DOMException is not properly handled by AVA's \`throwsAsync\`.`. That reason is what the comment in the file states; the inspected evidence does not itself verify a Node.js or AVA defect.

The two guarded tests are `clearQueue rejects pending promises when enabled`, built on `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: true})`, and `limitFunction exposes clearQueue`, built on `limitFunction(() => delay(20), {concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: true})`. Each asserts the already-running promise still resolves (`await runningPromise;`) while the pending promises reject with `{name: 'AbortError'}` through `t.throwsAsync(...)`.
